next_steps: Run aerators or add fresh, well-oxygenated water if available, and stop feeding until fish recover.
Reduce or pause feeding and re-test ammonia/nitrite within 24 hours; consider a partial water exchange.
Record which fish show signs and how many, take clear photos, and contact a fisheries officer. Do not start medication without professional advice.
Treat this as urgent: check the pond again within a few hours.
data.referral: This check is not a diagnosis. For suspected disease, unusual mortality or any medication or chemical treatment, consult a qualified fisheries officer (e.g. the local Department of Fisheries office or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra fisheries specialist) before acting.

threshold_profile.label: Generic warm-water pond aquaculture — demonstration settings
threshold_profile.applies_to: Warm-water freshwater finfish ponds (e.g. Indian major carps, tilapia, pangasius). Not tuned for shrimp, brackish water, hatcheries or any specific species.
threshold_profile.notes: Bands are informed by commonly cited general ranges in warm-water pond aquaculture literature (e.g. Boyd, C.E., Water Quality in Ponds for Aquaculture, 1990). The exact numbers in this file have NOT been checked against a specific published table for any species or for coastal Karnataka conditions. A qualified fisheries professional must review them before any real use.

data.disclaimer: Demonstration rules engine. Thresholds are unvalidated demonstration settings for generic warm-water ponds and do not diagnose disease.
